panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). C: Panel C is x20 IHC view of sebaceous epithelioma with MSH6 staining maintained, patient histopathology of MTS-associated sebaceous neoplasm. D: Panel D is x40 IHC view of sebaceous epithelioma with maintained MSH6 expression, patient histopathology of MTS-associated sebaceous neoplasm.

The epidermis adjacent to the tumor also shows positive staining for MSH6 (black arrows). The staining of the tumor cells (black triangles) shows that the expression of the MSH6 mismatch repair gene is maintained (immunoperoxidase stain: A, ×4; B, ×10; C, ×20; D, ×40).

plate_findings.evidence: sebaceous adenoma presenting as a papule on the nose - 1x1-millimeter, flesh-colored, smooth papule with a central umbilication on the right nostril

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Distant view panel A shows flesh-colored umbilicated papule on right nostril marked by black arrow in 59-year-old male with germline-confirmed MLH1-associated Lynch syndrome diagnosed as MLH1-associated Muir-Torre syndrome after biopsy showed sebaceous adenoma. B: Closer view panel B shows same sebaceous adenoma papule circled in purple ink in patient with MLH1-associated Muir-Torre syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen and Kurzrock. Germline Testing of Mismatch Repair Genes Is Needed in the Initial Evaluation of Patients With Muir-Torre Syndrome-Associated Cutaneous Sebaceous Neoplasms: A Case Series.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.33975. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 13.
panels.figure_caption: Sebaceous adenoma presenting as a papule on the nose of a 59-year-old male Abbreviation: MLH1, MutL Homolog 1 Distant (A) and closer (B) views of the right nostril show a lesion of four years duration appearing as a 1 × 1-millimeter, flesh-colored, smooth papule with a central umbilication on the right nostril (black arrow and within the purple-inked oval). The man had germline-confirmed MLH1-associated Lynch syndrome; he had an intramucosal adenocarcinoma (pTis) arising focally in a tubular adenoma located in his ascending colon diagnosed at age 53 years. His family history was significant for colorectal cancer (mother had two primary neoplasms), kidney cancer (brother), liver cancer (mother and father), pancreatic cancer (mother), and rectal cancer (brother). The diagnosis of MLH1-associated Muir-Torre syndrome was established after the microscopic evaluation of the lesion, which was completely removed during the punch biopsy using a 2-millimeter biopsy instrument, showed a sebaceous adenoma; immunohistochemistry analysis of the sebaceous tumor unexpectedly showed preservation of the MLH1 mismatch repair gene.
in_text_mentions: Cutaneous examination of his face showed a 1 × 1-millimeter, flesh-colored, smooth papule with a central umbilication on the right nostril (Figure 13). The clinical differential diagnosis included a fibrous papule, basal cell carcinoma, and sebaceous neoplasm, such as an adenoma or epithelioma. A punch biopsy, using a 2-millimeter biopsy instrument attempting to remove the entire lesion, was performed.

plate_findings.evidence: basaloid nodule with prominent sebaceous differentiation in the dermis (within the black oval)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E of chest sebaceous carcinoma in Muir-Torre case series; low-power basaloid nodule with sebaceous differentiation matches sebaceous carcinoma histology vocabulary, supported by disease-focused article title plus captioned manifestation. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E histology of a sebaceous adenoma from a Muir-Torre Syndrome patient (MSH6 germline variant), showing the classic dual basaloid/sebaceous architecture with cystic dilatation described in the caption and in-text; a hallmark cutaneous manifestation of MTS. [raw subtype: MSH6] B: High-power H&E of the same sebaceous adenoma showing germinative (basaloid) cell proliferation, the classic histologic pattern of a cutaneous sebaceous neoplasm in Muir-Torre Syndrome. [raw subtype: MSH6] C: Low-power H&E showing colonic adenocarcinoma adjacent to normal mucosa; the in-text localizes the tumor to the cecum (right-sided), a classic visceral manifestation of Muir-Torre Syndrome. [raw subtype: MSH6] D: High-power H&E of the cecal adenocarcinoma showing poorly differentiated glands with mucin production, consistent with the high-grade right-sided colorectal carcinoma typical of Muir-Torre Syndrome. [raw subtype: MSH6]

in_text_mentions: The multiple sebaceous adenomas histologically showed dermal tumors with varying proportions of basaloid cells and sebaceous cells with cystic changes (Figure 2A and B). The pathologic evaluation of the colonic tumor showed a 7.5 × 7.2 × 4.3 cm fungating mass within the cecum. Histologically, the tumor was a high-grade adenocarcinoma with mucin production and invading the subserosal adipose tissue. Tumor infiltrating lymphocytes or germinal centers were not seen (Figure 2C and D). Strong nuclear expression of MLH1, PMS2, and MLH2 mismatch repair proteins was seen in the adenocarcinoma by IHC.

in_text_mentions: e) also had a keratoacanthoma. This type of skin lesion is seen in some families with MSH2 or, less commonly, MLH1 mutations when it is termed Muir–Torre Syndrome (MTS) (Ponti and Ponz de Leon, 2005). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) at the time showed normal MSH2 expression, so we felt that this family did not belong to the MTS group. Subsequently, the individual was diagnosed with two separate sebaceous carcinomas on each arm. Immunohistochemistry analysis of these lesions shows loss of MSH2 expression in both cases, one of which is shown in Figure 1, confirming that this is in fact an MTS family.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E scanner view (10X) of the excisional biopsy from the reported case of extraocular sebaceous carcinoma in Lynch syndrome (article title: 'Extraocular Sebaceous Carcinoma in Lynch Syndrome: A Sentinel Cutaneous Clue to Muir-Torre Syndrome'). The caption and in-text describe multiple tumor lobules with peripheral squamous differentiation (black arrow) and central sebaceous morphology (green arrow), matching the sebaceous carcinoma histology finding; sebaceous carcinoma is a defining cutaneous manifestation of Muir-Torre syndrome. The image is a real patient histology slide with arrow annotations and no third-party restriction. Age and ethnicity are not stated in the caption or the provided in-text, and skin tone is not assessable on histology, so those fields are null/unknown. The organized dual squamous-sebaceous differentiation is treated as a recognized less common (variant) histologic form, and the peripheral squamous component is added as a proposed finding since no vocabulary entry captures it separately. [raw subtype: extraocular]

in_text_mentions: The lesion was friable and bled upon palpation. Multiple seborrheic keratoses of varying sizes were also observed on the patient’s face. Given the rapid growth of the lesion, an excisional biopsy was performed for histopathological examination. Differential diagnoses considered included seborrheic keratosis, verruca (wart), pyogenic granuloma, and SC. Histopathological examination of the biopsy sample revealed multiple tumor lobules with characteristic peripheral squamous differentiation and central sebaceous morphology (Figure 2).
